checks: Matched the argument to original candidate 8db47b3dd5d8d71d §2, equation (4), and verified the raw source digest. Dropping original-weight monotonicity is justified because log-concavity controls the ratios without any bound on them by one.

For i<N the terms of S_(i+1)/w_(i+1) at h=0,…,N−i−1 are bounded termwise by those of S_i/w_i by sliding the product of h mass ratios one place right. The latter has the additional strictly positive term w_N/w_i, including the final i=N−1 comparison. Taking reciprocals gives strict increase of the hazard and hence strict decrease of the survival ratios through the terminal ratio zero.

When i+k≤N all denominators and all factors for k≥1 are positive. For i,k>0 every shifted factor is strictly smaller than the corresponding unshifted factor. When i+k>N the unnormalized left-hand tail is zero, with a strict inequality exactly when both right-hand tails are positive. The axes i=0 and k=0 give identities, and if either tail vanishes then the product and left tail vanish.

For N=0 the ratio sequence consists of zero and the strict submultiplicativity condition is vacuous. For N=1 the two ratios are strictly ordered, and i=k=1 gives a zero left-hand tail against a positive product.
Cross-checked with 462 positive rational profiles of length at most seven generated by nonincreasing mass ratios from {1/3,1/2,1,2,3}, including increasing weights and tail indices past the support.

overlap.comparison: Its proof gives the nonstrict ratio monotonicity and submultiplicativity for any finite consecutive-support log-concave law. Normalize by M and start the support at 0 to recover its weak bound here. It does not record the strict comparison from the additional endpoint term.

Its moment argument likewise states only the weak ratio and product comparisons for finite consecutive-support laws, possibly starting after 0. The candidate isolates the strict finite-support strengthening on positive tails.

readability: In the i+k>N case, ‘the left side’ refers to S_(i+k) in the original inequality, which avoids dividing by a zero S_i.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The finite right endpoint forces strict survival-ratio decrease and strict submultiplicativity when both positive-index tails remain positive.
